requirement_text.REQ-459:
Source: GH #2335 (ISS-1039, Q-1021, requirement C: required decision outputs) and GH #2323 (ISS-1034, Q-1016, requirement A: distinct person). Both rules add a refusal to the same function, Letflow.Engine.run_complete_task (lib/letflow/engine.ex, near line 2263), so they share ONE design pass. This entry writes a design artefact only, in lib/letflow/design/, no application code (CODE-DESIGNER is design-only). Read first: lib/letflow/engine.ex (run_complete_task and merge_output_variables/7), lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex, lib/letflow/engine/variable_schema.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex (node-attribute checks, CHK-20 form schema, CHK-21 escalation pair), lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex, lib/letflow/tasks.ex (claim_task/3, assign_task/4, reassign_task/4), lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex, lib/letflow/design/req396-human-task-escalation-timer.md, lib/letflow/design/req455-definition-validator-gaps.md, docs/migration/decisions/0007-variable-merge-validates-new-keys.md, the self_approval_forbidden precedent in lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex (approve_review).
BINDING CONSTRAINTS from the design-intent owner (letflow-9a). The design implements them and does not re-decide them.
Rule A, distinct person: - identity is the USER ID, never the role; this also holds for a
  request made with an API token (the identity is the token's user);
- enforced at COMPLETION (the authority) and at CLAIM (early
  feedback only);
- NO role is exempt, TENANT_ADMIN included; - the comparison is against the MOST RECENT completion of each
  named node in the same instance, so rework loops work;
- the node attribute is OPTIONAL and OFF by default: a definition
  without it behaves exactly as before;
- the refusal is a clean 4xx with zero detail beyond 'separation of
  duties';
- the REQ-455 validator WARNS (not a violation) when distinct_from
  names a node that routes to the same single-member role (that node
  could never complete); this is the validator entry's rule
  (REQ-464), the design only specifies its inputs;
- PROCESS-AUDITOR checklist item B1 (.claude/agents/process-auditor.md
  and its docs) may answer YES when the attribute is present: that
  text change is a follow-up recorded in the open_questions of
  REQ-463, not part of any engine change.

Rule C, required decision outputs: - the check runs on the SERVER BEFORE any state change; - a form's `required` flag stays a UI hint (REQ-273) and is never the
  control;
- the validator also flags a decision (edge condition or gateway)
  reading a key that no upstream task declares in required_outputs;
- an out-of-enum value (any value a variable_schema rejects on this
  path) is a retryable 422 and NO instance ERROR; the refusal happens
  before anything is written, so the task stays open and claimable.

THE DESIGN MUST DECIDE AND STATE, each as a numbered section: 1. Definition schema: where `required_outputs` (list of variable
   keys) and `distinct_from` (list of node ids) live in a HUMAN_TASK
   node (the existing node attributes map, next to role,
   escalation_timer_duration, escalation_role and form_schema), their
   types, and the validator code names reserved for REQ-461 and
   REQ-464.
2. ONE check order inside run_complete_task, as a numbered list:
   where the distinct-person check and the required-outputs and
   schema-rejection checks sit relative to the task and instance
   row locks, the form-expression re-evaluation and merge_output_variables/7,
   and why no write precedes the first refusal. State how a refusal
   that must roll back the Multi still leaves exactly one audited
   refusal record (the record must not live inside the rolled-back
   transaction).
3. The 422 body for rule C: error code, missing required key names,
   rejected key names; no submitted value, no enum list, no instance
   or other-task data. The retry contract (what the client resends).
4. The refusal body and status for rule A: one fixed body, identical
   whichever node or user caused it, carrying nothing beyond
   'separation of duties'. Choose the status among the 4xx codes and
   justify it against the existing error-contract of
   Letflow.Routers.Tasks.
5. The audit record of a refusal for both rules: fields, with no PII
   (no submitted values, no names, no emails), and where it is
   written.
6. Claim path for rule A (Letflow.Tasks.claim_task/3): the same
   comparison as early feedback. DECIDED (BA, 2026-10-07):
   assign_task/4 and reassign_task/4 do NOT check distinct_from;
   completion is the authority, so an administrator may assign a task
   to anyone and the completion check still refuses a person who
   already completed a named node.
7. API-token identity: which value reaches run_complete_task as
   actor_id for a token request, shown by a file and line, and a
   statement that the comparison uses it.
8. Rework semantics: how 'most recent completion of a named node in
   this instance' is read from stored data (which table or events),
   and the read cost. DECIDED (BA, 2026-10-07): a named node that has
   not completed in this instance (the path skipped it, or a timer
   escalated past it) imposes no constraint. DECIDED: the named nodes
   may lie on PARALLEL branches with no path between them; the check
   compares the actor with the completions that exist AT THE TIME of
   the check, in any order, so whichever of two parallel nodes
   completes later must differ from the earlier completer.
9. Interaction with D-ESC escalation tasks (REQ-396: a timer on a
   HUMAN_TASK creates an escalation task and cancels or supersedes
   the original) and with timer cancellation: whether an escalation
   task inherits its source node's distinct_from, whether completing
   the escalation task counts as a completion of the source node for
   other nodes' distinct_from, and what happens to a claim made
   before the timer fired.
10. Interaction with the idempotency key and a replayed completion:
   a replay of an already-accepted completion by the same user is not
   refused by rule A.
11. How each rule leaves the service-task and other engine-internal
   merge paths unchanged, and the exact amendment of REQ-061's text
   and the 0007 passages (see REQ-460's open_questions).
12. Test plan skeleton per rule: the negative cases, the API-token
   case, the rework-loop case, TENANT_ADMIN not exempt, the
   default-off case.
DECIDED (BA, 2026-10-07), not open: FormExpressionReevaluation errors (build_reevaluation_execution_error_args in engine.ex) are unchanged on this path and still end in EXECUTION_ERROR, because they are definition defects and not caller input.
requirement_text.REQ-460:
Source: GH #2335 (ISS-1039, Q-1021). Today a HUMAN_TASK can be completed without its decision key: variable_schemas (REQ-109) validate only the keys that ARE submitted and the form_schema `required` list is a UI hint (REQ-273), so an omitted decision follows the fail-closed route silently and the operator's intent is lost. Also today any value a variable_schema rejects (for example an out-of-enum decision) puts the WHOLE instance into ERROR through the merge path (REQ-061), so one bad value from any task worker halts a business case. Implement exactly the design of REQ-459 (read it first; where this text and the design differ on a detail the design wins and the difference is reported).
BUILDS (what, not how; the design owns the how): 1. HUMAN_TASK node attribute `required_outputs: [keys]`, read by
   Letflow.Engine.run_complete_task (lib/letflow/engine.ex).
2. A completion-time check on the SERVER, before any state change: a
   completion whose SUBMITTED output_variables lack a required key
   (absent or null; a value already held by the instance from an
   earlier pass does not count) is refused with a retryable 422 whose
   body names the missing keys. The task stays open and claimable,
   the instance, tokens, variables and events are unchanged, and the
   only write is one audited refusal record without PII.
3. A value that a variable_schema rejects on the HUMAN_TASK
   completion path (out-of-enum, wrong type) is refused the same way:
   retryable 422 naming the rejected keys, no instance ERROR, nothing
   written. A form's `required` flag stays a UI hint.
DECIDED (BA, 2026-10-07): a required key whose submitted value is null counts as missing; an empty string is judged by the variable_schema's own type and enum rules. DECIDED: form-expression re-evaluation errors are unchanged (still EXECUTION_ERROR).
4. Engine-internal merges (service-task outputs, REQ-056 and
   others) keep going through the EXECUTION_ERROR / REQ-061 path
   unchanged; merge/3 and its whole-batch semantics are unchanged.

EXPLICIT AMENDMENT OF ACCEPTED BEHAVIOUR. REQ-061 (status done) lists among the callers of the shared ERROR sink 'REQ-049's schema-violation-on-merge case'. After this entry that case still routes to ERROR for service-task and other engine-internal merges, but NOT for a HUMAN_TASK completion: there a rejected output is a retryable 422 with no state change and no EXECUTION_ERROR event. REQ-061's text is therefore amended, not contradicted, and DOC-UPDATER leaves a dated amendment pointer on REQ-061 (see acceptance criteria). Tests that today assert instance ERROR after a HUMAN_TASK completion with a rejected output (search test/letflow/engine_complete_task_test.exs, test/letflow/engine/shipped_definition_variable_schemas_engine_test.exs, test/letflow/engine/variable_schema_test.exs) are changed to the new behaviour, each with a comment citing this entry.
DECISION RECORD 0007 (docs/migration/decisions/0007-variable-merge-validates-new-keys.md) is NOT edited by this entry. It is flagged below for REVIEWER sign-off, per the decision-record rule.
requirement_text.REQ-461:
Source: GH #2335 (ISS-1039, Q-1021) scope item (1) and the design-intent constraint 'the validator also flags a decision reading a key no upstream task declares in required_outputs'. Adds deterministic checks beside the existing node-attribute checks in lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex (CHK-20 form schema, CHK-21 escalation pair) and the data-flow checks in lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex (REQ-455), using the violation code names reserved in the REQ-459 design.
BUILDS: 1. Shape check: `required_outputs` on a HUMAN_TASK is a list of
   non-empty strings without duplicates; on any other node type the
   attribute is a violation.
2. Every key in required_outputs has a variable_schema in the
   definition's variable_schemas, or the check reports the node and the
   key (the enum or type is what keeps the value valid, REQ-109).
3. Decision reads: for an edge condition or exclusive gateway that
   reads a variable key, report it when the key IS the output of a
   HUMAN_TASK on the path (appears in that task's form_schema
   properties) and NO upstream HUMAN_TASK on any path declares it in
   required_outputs. Whether this is a violation or a warning, and
   which keys count as decision keys, is fixed by the REQ-459 design;
   this entry builds what the design says and no more.
4. Run wherever the existing checks run (validate, activate, import).
requirement_text.REQ-463:
Source: GH #2323 (ISS-1034, Q-1016, BA checklist B2). Distinct roles do not stop ONE person who holds several roles, or the same role, from completing several steps of the SAME instance (meridian loan l1, l2, committee votes, D-ESC escalation, disbursement; the regulatory sign-off chain; vortex and swiftroute approvals). Precedent: self_approval_forbidden in lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex (approve_review). Implement exactly the REQ-459 design and slot the check into the order REQ-460 established in run_complete_task.
BINDING CONSTRAINTS (design-intent owner letflow-9a; not to be re-decided here): - identity is the USER ID, never the role; for an API-token request
  the identity is the token's user;
- enforced at COMPLETION as the authority and at CLAIM
  (Letflow.Tasks.claim_task/3) as early feedback;
- NO role is exempt, TENANT_ADMIN included; - the completing user is compared against the MOST RECENT completion
  of each named node in the same instance, so rework loops work;
- BA decision 2026-10-07: a named node may lie on a PARALLEL branch
  (no path between the nodes); the check compares with the
  completions that exist at the time of the check, in any order, so
  whichever parallel node completes later must differ from the
  earlier completer; a named node that has not completed (path
  skipped, timer escalated past it) imposes no constraint;
- the attribute is OPTIONAL and OFF by default: definitions without it
  behave identically;
- the refusal is a clean 4xx with zero detail beyond 'separation of
  duties'.

BUILDS: 1. HUMAN_TASK node attribute `distinct_from: [node ids]`. 2. Completion check in Letflow.Engine.run_complete_task: if the actor
   is the user who most recently completed any listed node in this
   instance, refuse with the REQ-459 refusal body. Nothing is written
   except one audited refusal record without PII; the task stays open
   and claimable.
3. Claim check in Letflow.Tasks.claim_task/3 with the same comparison
   and the same refusal body.
4. Out of scope: org-chart or delegation models, a tenant-wide
   switch. DECIDED (BA, 2026-10-07): assign_task/4 and
   reassign_task/4 do not check distinct_from; the completion check
   still refuses.
requirement_text.REQ-464:
Source: GH #2323 (ISS-1034, Q-1016): 'the process validator checks that the referenced nodes exist and precede the node', AMENDED by BA decision 2026-10-07: a named node may lie on a PARALLEL branch (no path between the two nodes); strict precedence applies only when the named node is on the same path as this node. Plus the design-intent constraint that the REQ-455 validator WARNS (not a violation) when distinct_from names a node that routes to the same single-member role (the node could never complete). Adds checks beside the existing node-attribute checks in lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex and the install-time role warnings added by REQ-455 (unbound task roles are reported as a warning list, never an automatic binding).
BUILDS: 1. Shape: `distinct_from` on a HUMAN_TASK is a list of non-empty node
   ids without duplicates and without the node's own id; on any other
   node type it is a violation.
2. Existence: every listed id is a node of the same definition and a
   HUMAN_TASK; a missing id is a violation naming node and id.
3. Path position: a listed node must not be reachable only AFTER this
   node (this node has a path to it and it has no path to this node):
   a node downstream-only is a violation naming both, since it can
   never have completed when this node is checked. A listed node
   that precedes this node, is on a parallel branch (no path either
   way) or is on a rework loop (a path both ways) passes.
4. Same-role WARNING: when this node and a listed node route to the
   same role and that role has exactly one member in the installing
   tenant, the validation result carries a WARNING (not a violation)
   naming both nodes and the role, because the single member could
   never complete the second node. Evaluated where tenant role
   membership is known (install or activate), as REQ-455 check 4 is;
   at pure definition validation without a tenant it is not evaluated.
